elements.element: Services are performed in a professional manner.
elements.evidence: The clause requires reasonable care measured against the Servicer's own treatment of comparable receivables, but does not impose an objective professional-performance standard.

elements.element: Services are performed in a workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: Neither the existing servicing standard nor the added warranty expressly requires workmanlike performance.
The added warranty requires conformity only "in all material respects," permitting immaterial nonconformities not permitted by the preferred position.

elements.element: Non-software deliverables conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: The warranty covers software and receivables systems, not deliverables generally.

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts at least 12 months after delivery.
elements.evidence: The software warranty lasts only 90 days after delivery.

elements.element: The services warranty lasts at least 90 days after performance.
elements.evidence: The express services warranty lasts only 30 days after performance.

elements.element: Repair is available as a remedy for breach of the performance warranty.
elements.evidence: The Servicer must, at the Issuer's option, repair the non-conforming software, system, or services.

elements.element: Replacement is available as a remedy for breach of the performance warranty.
elements.evidence: The Issuer may require replacement of the non-conforming software, system, or services.

elements.element: Refund is available as a remedy for breach of the performance warranty.
elements.evidence: The Issuer may require a refund of the Servicing Fee paid for the affected software, system, or services.

elements.element: The Servicer complies with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: Section (ix) is phrased as past compliance and excuses violations that would not reasonably be expected to have a Material Adverse Effect; it does not provide unqualified, ongoing legal compliance.

elements.element: Software and deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: There is no malicious-code warranty or prohibition.

elements.element: Software is covered by a documentation-conformance warranty.
elements.evidence: The Servicer warrants that software and receivables systems will conform in all material respects to their documentation.

elements.element: The software warranty lasts at least 90 days after delivery.
elements.evidence: The warranty expressly applies for 90 days after delivery.

elements.element: Services are covered by a performance or conformance warranty.
elements.evidence: The Servicer warrants that its servicing and other services will conform to the Agreement and the Servicing Procedures.

elements.element: The services warranty lasts at least 30 days after performance.
elements.evidence: The warranty expressly applies for 30 days after performance.

elements.element: Repair is available as a remedy for breach of the software or services warranty.
elements.evidence: Repair is available at the Issuer's option for non-conforming software, systems, or services.

elements.element: Replacement is available as a remedy for breach of the software or services warranty.
elements.evidence: Replacement is available at the Issuer's option for non-conforming software, systems, or services.

elements.element: Refund is available as a remedy for breach of the software or services warranty.
elements.evidence: The Issuer may elect a refund of the Servicing Fee paid for the affected software, system, or services.

result.reason: The operative language reaches the fallback durations and remedies but not the preferred professional/workmanlike standard, 12-month software period, 90-day services period, unqualified legal-compliance obligation, or malicious-code warranty. It is not minimal because it unnecessarily relocates existing subsections and uses a broad service-conformity warranty. That broad warranty also risks contradicting the retained sole-remedy provision: a breach of Sections 3.2(c) or (d) could simultaneously be a failure of services to conform to the Agreement, making both acquisition and repair, replacement, or refund purported remedies. Numbering order and references to repairing or replacing services further reduce drafting quality.
